verdict:
RUNG PASSES: one call, identical thresholds, no per-readout tuning, reproduces both of the project's own verdicts -- lambda_ca NOT_DECIDABLE, top1 MODEL_DETERMINED at F130's published 0.848 and +0.752 to the digit. The packaged discriminator is faithful to the analysis it replaces. The binding branch for each readout is printed below rather than asserted here: lambda_ca was expected to bind on the unrankable-spread step and in fact binds one step earlier, on signal (2 of 4 constructions), which is what F129 reported first. Same label, different reason, and the reason is the part a reader needs.
  lambda_ca  -> NOT_DECIDABLE            expected NOT_DECIDABLE            ok
             lambda_ca: 2/4 constructions carry signal above seed noise; the construction moves it 2.9x more than the model does. NOT_DECIDABLE
             signal on only 2 of 4 constructions: model identity does not move lambda_ca beyond seed noise on a majority of the grid, so there is nothing for the construction axis to be tested against
  top1       -> MODEL_DETERMINED         expected MODEL_DETERMINED         ok
             top1: 6/6 constructions carry signal above seed noise; seed-stable ranking +0.848; cross-construction agreement +0.752; the construction moves it 0.7x more than the model does. DECIDED
             signal on 6/6 constructions, seed-stable ranking +0.848, and cross-construction agreement +0.752 >= 0.6: different constructions rank the models the same way, so top1 is model-attributable ACROSS THESE CONSTRUCTIONS
  nuisance gate, 24 cells with a stored period census: PASSES -- top1 equals its value under the mean 1/period of its settled replicas (F136) on 0 of 24 cells (0.0%, gate 25%)
             F136 measured 2 crystal replicas of 384, so the known answer is BENIGN and a gate that fired here would be too tight.
